evidence.title: OpenSpec supported tools
evidence.finding: OpenSpec installs skills and commands into coding assistant directories including Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, OpenCode and Pi. These are workflow integrations, not a hosted agent runtime.

evidence.locator: propose; apply; update; sync; verify; bulk archive
evidence.finding: Skills explore ideas, draft plans, edit requirements, check task boxes, verify implementation and archive changes. Verify is report-only; update asks for confirmation before artifact revisions.

evidence.title: OpenSpec project configuration
evidence.locator: How it works; context; rules; operations
evidence.finding: Project YAML injects context and artifact-specific rules into agent prompts; operations guide apply/archive. Config edits take effect on the next workflow run and are instructions, not enforced execution policy.

evidence.title: OpenSpec default schema
evidence.locator: Artifacts; drafting order; delta specs; tasks
evidence.finding: Proposal, delta specifications, design and task checklist are durable files. Artifact readiness follows schema dependencies; specs have requirements and scenarios; archive merges deltas into canonical specs.

evidence.finding: Stores separate shared planning into a Git repository and support read-only upstream references. Users push/pull themselves; stale checkouts remain stale. Stores are beta.

evidence.finding: Telemetry stores an anonymous identifier and notice state. Disable telemetry.enabled or set OPENSPEC_TELEMETRY=0 or DO_NOT_TRACK=1.

evidence.finding: Says OpenSpec is MIT licensed and mentions no paid plan.

evidence.title: Fission-AI/OpenSpec LICENSE (MIT)
evidence.finding: The MIT License lets anyone obtain, use, copy and modify the software free of charge.

evidence.title: OpenSpec docs: Supported Tools
evidence.locator: docs/supported-tools.md lines 3-10 (How It Works) and Tool Directory Reference lines 65-105, commit 579fcac
evidence.finding: openspec init writes OpenSpec skills and command files into each selected assistant's own directory; the user then invokes the workflow inside that assistant, so OpenSpec runs within the assistant's existing session rather than its own runtime or login.

evidence.title: OpenSpec: src/cli/index.ts
evidence.locator: Command registrations and imported command implementations; package.json bin/files; src/core/view.ts dashboard
evidence.finding: The released package exposes the openspec terminal CLI and Markdown workflow skills. Its command graph reads and writes project artifacts; it ships no desktop application, browser server or phone application. The view command prints status and progress to the terminal, not code diffs. Searches across src, skills and package.json for createServer, listen, spawn, worktree, docker, VM, scheduler, SAML and agent sessions found no agent runtime, workspace sandbox, co-prompting service or team identity layer. Child processes cover installation, Git store operations and editor/config helpers, not coding-agent sessions.

evidence.title: OpenSpec: skills/openspec-apply-change/SKILL.md
evidence.finding: The apply skill tells the existing assistant to read instructions and implement tasks from local project files. OpenSpec does not start or coordinate agent sessions. The installed CLI and skills have no schedule/event runner. Execution, parallel agent work and remote continuation depend on the assistant environment rather than an OpenSpec-managed executor.

evidence.title: OpenSpec: src/core/config.ts
evidence.locator: AI_TOOLS registry, available=true entries; docs/supported-tools.md shared agents target
evidence.finding: The shipped tool registry includes Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Pi, Grok Build and Antigravity. OpenSpec writes workflow skills for these tools. A vendor-neutral .agents target lets other compatible agents consume skills, so omission of Aider is not an explicit incompatibility.

evidence.title: OpenSpec: docs/stores-beta/user-guide.md
evidence.locator: The shape; Two rules; Sharing work is git, on purpose
evidence.finding: A store is an ordinary Git repository shared by user-managed commits, pushes, pulls and reviews. The source contains no multi-user prompting session, workspace role permissions or enterprise SSO; Git host permissions and review tools remain external.
